To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

KRAS mutations, but also BRAF mutations, NRAS mutations and PIK3Ca exon 20 mutations predict resistance to anti EGFR monoclonal antibodies, and that additional testing for these mutations may improve response rates in patients with KRAS wt tumors
KRAS, BRAFR, NRAS, PIK3CA, and BRAFV600E are all associated with a worse response to cetuximab.
KRAS, BRAFA, and NRAS mutations are associated with a low rate of response to cetuximab.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drugs and new combinations for the treatment of patients with colorectal cancer, in particular those with KRAS mutations.

the development and evaluation of new methods for the detection of genetic alterations in cancer cells and the application of these new technologies in clinical practice for the benefit of patients with cancer.
the study of the molecular basis of the response to the monoclonal antibody cetuximab and the effect of downstream mutations on outcome after treatment of metastatic colorectal carcinoma with cetuxim
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
KRAS mutations are a negative prognostic marker in colorectal cancer patients treated with cetuiximab and chemotherapy.
the combination of KRAS, NRAS, BRAF and PIK3Ca exon 20 and 9 mutations is the best predictor of the efficacy of cetoximab.
the presence of KRAS mutation in metastatic colorectal cancers is a negative predictor of response to EGFR-targeting agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that KRAS is still the most important predictive marker in colorectal cancer for the response to anti-EGFR therapy.
KRAS is the most important predictive biomarker for cetuximab and panitumumah, BRAF is the second, and NRAS and PIK3A are less important.
we have shown the effect of KRAS, NRAS, BRAF and PIK3A mutations on the outcome of chemotherapy refractory metastastic colorectal cancer patients treated with cetaximab plus chemotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
KRAS, BRAFI/II, PIK3CA, and NRAS mutations are not only prognostic factors, but also predictive markers of response to anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies (cetuximab and panitumumah).

the KRAS mutation status is the only molecular biomarker that is predictive for the efficacy of cetuimab plus chemotherapy, and that the other mutations are only associated with a lower response rate.
the response rates to anti-EGFR therapy are significantly lower in colorectal cancer patients with BRAF mutations than in patients with BRAF wild-type tumors.
